messages.author: af44a577d9ff08de
messages.subject: Using packrat with Hudson-CI
parts:
Hi,

We have started building R-packages from our company github repository using Hudson. When building a package, it is desirable to access packages from both CRAN like repositories and public github. We use packrat for this as follows:
  • create a packrat project locally with the private libraries and sources ignored by version control
  • push the package to github
  • clone the package to Hudson and `restore()` it
  • build the package from the private libraries
Just wondering if this seems like a fair usage of packrat? Was it intended to be use like/for this?

Cheers,

Guy

messages.author: ab0d2be2ea8dabe8
messages.subject: Re: Using packrat with Hudson-CI
parts:
Hi Guy,

This is one of the 'expert' uses of packrat we envisioned :) Although the main use case for packrat is for 'local dependency management' and 'sharable sandboxing', we also developed packrat so that one could:

1. Infer project dependencies locally with packrat::snapshot(), and
2. Rebuild a project's library remotely with packrat::restore()

as necessary. This is useful, as you've seen, for build systems and the like.

Let me know if you encounter any road blocks in using packrat like this!

Thanks,
Kevin
